mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has fallen for two consecutive weeks (1.3 to -0.6 to -2.7). This negative momentum reflects an ongoing contraction in discretionary shopping and leisure trips that will persist without new stimulus, producing a lower mean RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC declined from 1.3 to -2.7 over last three weeks
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds the mean over the last 28 days despite the two-week prior decline trend.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT dropped from 9.1 to -3.0 over two weeks, a swing exceeding 10 points, consistent with newly imposed mobility restrictions. Such restrictions mechanically reduce access to retail venues, driving RETAIL_REC lower over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 10 points over two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT swung from 9.1 to -3.0 between t-2w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean does not decline over the next 2 weeks despite TRANSIT's sharp two-week drop exceeding the 10-point threshold.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM surged from 1.7 to 11.4 while PARKS collapsed from 5.0 to -12.1 in the same window. This joint pattern indicates households are shifting to essential-only stockpiling behavior and abandoning outdoor/leisure activity simultaneously, compounding the suppression of discretionary RETAIL_REC visits beyond what either series alone would predict.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises more than 8 points while PARKS falls more than 15 points in the same 2-week window
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from 1.7 to 11.4 as PARKS fell from 5.0 to -12.1
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to decline over the next 2 weeks even when both the GROCERY_PHARM surge and PARKS collapse thresholds are simultaneously met.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility plateaued and began declining (11.9 to 9.7) while RESIDENTIAL mobility rose back toward zero (-2.0 to 0.0), indicating a shift toward stay-at-home behavior consistent with a lockdown regime. Under this regime, RETAIL_REC will remain suppressed over the next four weeks as commuting-linked and incidental retail trips do not recover.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from 11.9 to 9.7 while RESIDENTIAL rose from -2.0 to 0.0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean rises over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES continuing to decline and RESIDENTIAL staying flat or rising, invalidating the stay-at-home linkage.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has been highly volatile and net negative (-3.9, 5.0, -16.4, -12.1), suggesting a seasonal shift away from outdoor activity as weather turns less favorable. This reduces combined outdoor-and-retail outings, pulling RETAIL_REC down over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mean over trailing 2 weeks falls below -10
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS averaged -14.25 over the last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next week even though the trailing two-week PARKS mean remains below -10.

mechanism_narrative: As GROCERY_PHARM visits rise sharply, households are substituting essential shopping trips for discretionary retail outings, reallocating a fixed mobility budget away from RETAIL_REC categories over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose steadily from 1.7 to 11.4 across the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next week despite continued elevated or rising GROCERY_PHARM levels, indicating no substitution effect.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT turned negative (-3.0) after three weeks of positive readings, crossing from growth into contraction. This crossing signals reduced commuter and transit-dependent shopper traffic, which directly feeds into lower retail footfall the following week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT crosses from positive to negative week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from 3.0 to -3.0 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline in the week immediately following a TRANSIT sign flip from positive to negative.

mechanism_narrative: Joint decline in both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES over the last two weeks indicates coordinated restriction measures affecting both commuting and movement broadly. The interaction of these two suppressed channels amplifies the drop in RETAIL_REC beyond either series acting alone, sustaining lower retail mobility over a full four-week horizon.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both decline for two consecutive weeks simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from 9.1 to -3.0 and WORKPLACES fell from 11.9 to 9.7 over the same two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean does not fall over the next 28 days even though both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES continue declining together, refuting the compounding interaction.
